cat > /workspace/project/README.md <<'EOF'
# H3Act offline evidence pipeline

Run `python3 -B main.py` with a single JSON document on stdin. Pydantic and its
pinned dependencies are preinstalled; no network, model, certificate or service
configuration is needed. Read `../PROTOCOL.md` and `../RUNTIME.md` for the
contract.

## Layout

| File | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `main.py` | strict input decoding/validation, template compilation, orchestration |
| `schema.py` | typed payload models (`FuzzingPayload`, `H3HeaderFrame`, `H3DataFrame`, `H3SleepFrame`) |
| `HTTP3_Just_Send.py` | `HttpClient` request/event core against the injected offline backend |
| `modules/byte_program.py` | compressed byte sequences, byte expressions and templates |
| `modules/fuzz_adapter.py` | `FuzzExecutor` frame conversion, `OfflineTransport` receipts |
| `modules/clock.py` | socket-free coroutine scheduler with virtual time priorities |
| `modules/events.py` | decoded event records consumed by the client |
| `modules/capture_audit.py` | HTTP/1.1 origin framing, provenance and paired flags |

## Pipeline

1. `main.compile_document` validates the whole document (keys, types, budgets,
   ranges) and compiles every frame/event/part template through
   `byte_program.Context`, which evaluates the byte-expression grammar with
   CPython's `ast` and expands `<<random_string>>` markers.
2. `schema.compile_cases` wraps the compiled frames in the pydantic payload
   models; `FuzzExecutor.send_payload` converts them for `HttpClient`, which
   replays each case as a coroutine on `modules.clock.Clock` with the
   documented equal-time priorities (case starts, external events, pause
   completions, timeouts).
3. `OfflineTransport` records the exact sent/received receipts, fingerprints
   and counters for each case, including send errors after request end and
   events retained before termination.
4. `capture_audit.audit_channels` concatenates each channel's parts as a
   compressed rope, parses consecutive HTTP/1.1 requests with bounded head
   windows (body fingerprints come from rope arithmetic, never from expanded
   bytes) and derives `owner`/`owners`, request flags and the paired case
   diagnostics, enforcing the request and chunk-size line budgets.

Byte sequences are ropes (`leaf`/`concat`/`repeat`) that cache their length and
the protocol fingerprint `sum((b[i]+1)*257**(N-1-i)) mod 2**64`, so very large
captures and repeated boundary probes are audited without storing expanded
contents. Only bounded windows (line/block limits) are materialized.

The CLI reads one UTF-8 JSON object and writes one JSON object; every
documented rejection produces exactly `{"error":"input"}` with exit status 0.
EOF
